title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
constraints: Tree is given as a level-order array; use -1 to represent null nodes
description:
Given the root of a binary tree (as a **level-order array**), return its **maximum depth**.

The maximum depth is the number of nodes along the longest path from the root node down to the farthest leaf node.

**Tree encoding:** Nodes are given in level-order (BFS order). Use `-1` to represent a missing (`null`) child.

```text
Level-order: [3, 9, 20, -1, -1, 15, 7]

        3          <- depth 1
       / \
      9  20        <- depth 2
        /  \
       15   7      <- depth 3

Answer: 3
```

tests.explanation: Tree has root 1 with only a right child 2.
